html:
Carthage was a city in today's Tunisia, founded by Phoenician settlers from Tyre, that grew into a sea empire ruling much of the western Mediterranean until Rome destroyed it in 146 BCE. Its name means "New City". The traditional founding date is 814 BCE; archaeology points to the late ninth century BCE.

Legend says it was founded by Dido, a princess who fled Tyre. As the Phoenician cities in the east fell under Assyria and Persia, Carthage became the leader of the Phoenician colonies in the west, among them Gadir in Spain.

At its height it held:

  • The coast of North Africa and the farmland around the city.
  • Sardinia, western Sicily, the Balearic Islands and parts of southern Spain, with its silver mines.
  • A large navy and a great double harbour at home.

It was a republic run by elected magistrates and a council of rich families, and it fought largely with hired soldiers. For centuries it fought the Greek cities of Sicily, above all Syracuse.

Then it met Rome. In the First Punic War (264 to 241 BCE) it lost Sicily. In the Second Punic War (218 to 201 BCE) Hannibal crossed the Alps and won great victories in Italy, but Carthage lost in the end. It recovered its wealth, and the Roman Republic chose to finish it. In 146 BCE, after a three-year siege, Rome destroyed the city and sold its people into slavery. Rome later rebuilt Carthage as a Roman city, one of the largest in the empire.
